newsitem.title: USA: FBI ready to assist in California mass suicide case.
newsitem.headline: FBI ready to assist in California mass suicide case.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno said Thursday the FBI would be ready to help state and local law enforcement agencies after the discovery of 39 bodies in a California mansion in what police called an apparent mass suicide.
"The FBI is working with state and local law enforcement in monitoring the situation," she said at her weekly Justice Department news briefing.
"I don't know whether there has been a request for assistance, but we stand ready to assist, and I understand the FBI is working with state and local law enforcement," Reno said.
She declined to say whether there was any indication a federal crime had been committed, adding it would be more appropriate for local authorities to comment.
But when pressed on what, if any, federal law might apply to mass suicides, Reno replied, "You never can tell what the circumstances are, and it would be inappropriate for me to comment prematurely."
Commander Alan Fulmer of the San Diego County Sheriff's Department said at an early-morning news conference the cause of death remained a mystery, but he ruled out gas poisoning.
Fulmer said he believed the 39 people took their own lives in a strange ritual that left them appearing as though they had died peacefully in their sleep.
